pattern.crimePattern: a man who faked his own death for the insurance threatens to "come back to life" and expose his wife; her father kills him at the river
pattern.notes: Fictional family, insurer and hospital. "Pseudocide" fraud is a familiar newspaper story in Kenya; no real case is retold. The grandfather is written with dignity. The forgery's flaw (a doctor retired years before he "signed") is shown, never how it was made.

facts.text: A man's body was found caught on a barge rope in the Sagana river on Monday morning; his fingerprints match a man registered dead two years ago.
Two days in the water, with a deep blow to the side of the head.
KSh 3,100 was still in his pocket.
At the landing where the Mukoya path meets the river: scuffed mud where two people stood.
Fingerprints: Elphas Shikanda, whose national ID was registered deceased two years ago.
Death certificate: "died in a road accident, Busia, Uganda", issued on a medical certificate from Tororo District Hospital.
Ugandan medical certificate of death: Tororo District Hospital, signed "Dr. S. Opio", with a rubber stamp.
A genuine certificate for a death abroad is issued on an embassy-endorsed report from the foreign hospital.
Tororo hospital records: no such patient, ever. Dr. S. Opio retired eight years before the date he "signed".
Lewis: he paid KSh 5 million to Mrs. Jane Mukoya. "She cried in my office. A memorial, no body; cremated in Kampala, she said."
Lewis was at a family wedding in Nairobi all Saturday.
Insurance claim form: Jane Mukoya, stamped received by the insurer; KSh 5,000,000 paid to her account only.
In the Mukoya back house: men's clothes and a razor.
In the back house: a Kerugoya hardware store payslip for "Elias Shikanda".
Pinned to the back-house wall: a shopping list in Jane's handwriting.
Mzee Laban's heavy knobbed walking stick, freshly scrubbed; a chip of river sand pressed into a crack in the knob.
Mama Rose: Jane was in the kitchen with her all Saturday evening.
Mama Njambi: at about 20:30 Mzee Laban walked past with his stick and a younger man, towards the river. He came back alone at about 21:15, walking fast.
Records: Jane's phone in the compound zone all Saturday evening.
Records: Elphas's own phone, in the back house, last active at 20:20 in the compound zone.
"Elias" to Hellen, Friday: "I'm leaving them. I'll have money by Monday. Pack."
Salon book and lodging: Hellen worked until 21:00 on Saturday, then stayed with a friend in Sagana.
The sand crew: Gichuki was at the crew's camp all Saturday night; a card game until 01:00.
Autopsy: one blow from a heavy rounded object before he entered the water; water in the lungs, so he was alive but unconscious when he went in.
Autopsy: death on Saturday between 20:30 and 22:00.
Autopsy: blood alcohol low; no strangulation; the wound is rounded, not a hull's edge.
Comparison view: the doctor who "signed" retired eight years earlier, and the hospital has no such patient.
Under the magnifier: the "Tororo" stamp is pressed rubber-stamp ink, not printer dots.
A medical certificate has no parcel, no exam index number, no chassis number.
There is no register entry to compare the doctor's signature with; that tell belongs to another document.
Lab: the sand in the stick's knob matches the landing where Mama Njambi saw them going.
Wilfrida Ayugi: the medical certificate is forged. The "Tororo" rubber stamp was made in Kenya: the font gives it away.

interrogations.intro: Jane sits in the main house in a widow's headscarf she has worn for two years. "My husband died two years ago in Uganda. I haven't seen him since."
Mzee Laban sits very calmly on the veranda, both hands on his knee. "I am an old man. I was in my house all evening."
Hellen stands at the salon door with a comb in her hand. "I don't know any Elphas Shikanda."
Gichuki wrings out his trouser legs. "He owed me 8,000 for sand. I found him. I didn't know it was him."
Lewis answers from Nairobi and goes quiet when you say the name.

contradictions.reaction: "We did it together. The debts were going to bury us. He lived at the back. On Friday he said half the money or he'd tell them it was me. My father heard him."
She looks at the photograph and drops the comb. "Elias. I knew him as Elias. He said he'd have money by Monday."

"I gave him my roof for two years. I hid him from the world for my daughter's sake. And he would send her to prison for money to spend on another woman. I took him to the river to talk. He laughed. I am not sorry for the stick. I am sorry the river did the rest."

reconstruction.text: Two years ago Elphas, drowning in debt, and his wife Jane fake his death: a road accident in Uganda, a forged Tororo medical certificate, a memorial with no body. The insurer pays Jane KSh 5 million.
Elphas lives in the back house of her father's compound as "Elias", works at a hardware store, and takes up with Hellen in Sagana.
Friday. He tells Jane he is leaving her for Hellen, and that unless she gives him half the money he will "come back to life" and tell the insurer it was all her idea. Mzee Laban hears it.
Saturday, about 20:30. Laban walks with Elphas down the river path "to talk like men". At the landing Elphas laughs at him. Laban strikes him with his heavy stick and pushes him into the river.
21:15. Laban walks back up the path alone, fast, and scrubs his stick. On Monday the sand harvesters find the body on a barge rope.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: a warrant on the back house and records on Jane. Detain Laban after his confession; the soil (8 h) and the medical-certificate examination (10 h) come back inside his 24 hours.

ui.beatNotes: A dead man's file. When the prints come back, a second case folder slides out of the cabinet: Elphas's two-year-old death record, stamped CLOSED. The player opens a closed file inside a live one, and the CLOSED stamp is struck through at the verdict.
